findings.title: Original argument and outer tools/call parameter keys can be erased before closed admission
findings.trigger: Start with any valid complete fictional tools/call argument record admitted by the direct SDK roundtrip. Add a tenth enumerable own argument named __proto__ with value null in the actual JSON text. Keep the nine required arguments, name, ID and bounded frame unchanged. JSON.parse creates this as an own data key; use actual JSON text or JSON.parse rather than an object-literal __proto__ setter.
source_only_path: ExpertFrameBuffer.readMessage parses the original JSON; accept() retains only scope and method, without original argument key validation or retention.
Locked Server.setRequestHandler wraps the handler in dispatchCodec.validateRequest and invokes it with outcome.value.
The locked legacy tools/call schema parses arguments as z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()). Zod4.6.5 record parsing explicitly continues over the __proto__ own key.

The application handler executes params.arguments from that projected value. argumentsRecord therefore sees exactly nine keys and cannot refuse the tenth original key. All nine required original values remain valid, so decode and the unchanged kernel can proceed.
findings.related_outer_params_trace: The same wrapper validates legacy CallToolRequestParamsSchema derived from default stripping z.object BaseRequestParamsSchema. An unknown outer params key such as unsupported_flag is dropped before the application Object.keys(params).length===2 check at400-405. Recognized _meta/task are different: they remain known schema keys and the handler can refuse them. Validate the original outer key set as well as the original nine argument keys in the same correction.
findings.expected_contract: Every extra original argument and disallowed outer tools/call parameter must stop before decode/kernel; both original closed key sets must be checked before any lossy SDK projection.
findings.predicted_not_executed: For the stated otherwise-valid wire request, the projected key set reaches captureExpertArguments and kernel rather than an ARGUMENTS refusal. This is a source-level contract counterexample; no JS/SDK/fixture/runtime execution was performed by this reviewer.
findings.impact: Closed wire-schema admission is bypassed for the extra original key. This finding does not claim prototype pollution, input value alteration, human validation, or a failing observed CI test.
findings.requested_narrow_correction: Admit the original raw-parsed tools/call params/arguments before SDK projection, or retain those original records by request ID and use them for the same closed admission in the handler. Add in-memory actual locked-SDK request regressions using an own __proto__ argument key constructed through JSON text and an unknown outer parameter; assert stable no-echo refusal, zero decode and zero kernel calls, plus a complete valid control. No extra spawned SDK child is necessary.
findings.existing_controls_limit: Direct argumentsRecord rejects an extra own key, but the direct extra/symbol/getter tests do not pass that raw record through the SDK record projection; there is no __proto__ fixture in the current frozen test file.
